{{Quote|You loathsome two-eyed toad!|Ree-Yees, to Bubo|<ref name="TT:BT">{{StoryCite|story=Tongue-tied: Bubo's Tale|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}}</ref>}}
'''Frog-dogs''' were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Reptile/Legends|lizards]] with both [[Frog/Legends|frog]]-like and [[Dog/Legends|dog]]-like features. Each member of the species had a large cranium that sported two large, protruding [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and long, pointed [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]] that stuck out from the mouth. Two squat [[Limb/Legends|limbs]] with five-fingered hands supported the body, although a frog-dog at rest kept his or her large, bulbous mid-section on the ground as well. The body tapered to a long, thin tail. Frog-dogs caught [[Insect/Legends|insects]] and other prey with a long, sticky tongue that darted from the mouth and retrieved the desired meal. The creatures hopped and waddled from place to place. Frog-dog vocalizations sounded like throaty barks and croaks.

Although they were both sentient and highly intelligent, frog-dogs were often mistaken for simple animals. They did nothing to change this misconception and sometimes even used it to their advantage. A frog-dog might deign to live as the pet of another sentient being, for example, trading a life of denigration for a guaranteed source of food. Others worked as [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]] and [[Spy/Legends|spies]], using their unassuming appearance to get into position to complete a particular mission. The frog-dog [[Buboicullaar/Legends|Buboicullaar]] operated in this manner as a "pet" of both a tribe of [[Jawa/Legends|Jawas]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] and of [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] in the [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord's]] [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|palace]]. While a member of Jabba's court, Buboicullaar plotted to kill his [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] master. Meanwhile, he foiled a similar assassination scheme by the [[Gran/Legends|Gran]] [[Ree-Yees/Legends|Ree-Yees]]. Upon Jabba's [[Death/Legends|death]] at the [[Great Pit of Carkoon/Legends|Great Pit of Carkoon]], Buboicullaar joined the [[B'omarr Order/Legends|B'omarr Order]].

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|Stupid two-eyed maggot fish! It's a good thing I don't need you anymore!|Ree-Yees, to Bubo, as the Gran's assassination plot against Jabba the Hutt progresses|<ref name="G:TTOR-Y" />}}
[[File:Bubo2_btm.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The frog-dog body included a bulbous head, protruding belly, and long, tapered tail.]]
Frog-dogs were [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]], [[Reptile/Legends|reptilian]]<ref name="CSWE I 296" /> [[amphibicanoid]]s<ref name="Wolf">{{StoryCite|story=Lone Wolf: A Tale of Obi-Wan and Luke|book=SkyeWalkers: A Clone Wars Story}}</ref> with features of both [[Frog/Legends|frogs]] and [[Dog/Legends|dogs]].<ref name="CSWE I 96">{{CSWECite|I|96|Bubo (Buboicullaar)}}</ref> They had two [[Limb/Legends|limbs]] that featured five-fingered hands with craggy [[gray]] nails.<ref name="WWIJP 86">{{InsiderCite|60|Who's Who in Jabba's Palace}}</ref><ref name="SSC">''[[Sideshow Collectibles]]'' {{C|Buboicullaar Creature Pack}}</ref> Nevertheless, the shortness and splayed arrangement of these appendages kept the frog-dog body low to the ground, making each member of the [[Species/Legends|species]] rest on his or her protuberant belly when at rest. In this position, most frog-dogs stood a mere 0.5 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall,<ref name="BTM" /> at which height a mass of 35 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]] was normal<ref name="HTHTT 36" />&mdash;although at least one specimen on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] grew to at least four times that size.<ref name="SNES" /> The body tapered to a long, thin tail toward the species' dorsal regions. Rows of bony lumps ran along the back and down the length of the tail.<ref name="BTM" /><ref name="SSC" /> Frog-dogs were covered in warty hides whose pigmentation varied from individual to individual:<ref name="G:TTOR-Y" /> possible [[Color/Legends|colorations]] included brown,<ref name="JTH:B" /> green,<ref name="BTM" /> orange-red,<ref name="SWR:O" /> purple,<ref name="CSW:ROTJ" /> and yellowish dun,<ref name="TUC" /> although boils, warts, and mottling of another color could appear as well.<ref name="BTM" /><ref name="EGC 132">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> Frog-dog skin hung loosely on the frame; coupled with their large warts, this created folds so deep that small objects could be hidden inside the flaps.<ref name="G:TTOR-Y" />

A huge cranium dominated the forequarters of a frog-dog's body.<ref name="TT:BT" /> Two bulbous, heavy-lidded, frog-like [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]<ref name="AGTTSWU2 70">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref><ref name="SWE 37">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> protruded from the top of the visage, their coloration varying from one frog-dog to the next. Possible hues included purple,<ref name="CSWE I 296" /> red,<ref name="SNES" /> and yellow.<ref name="SWR:O" /> Frog-dogs had excellent vision,<ref name="BTM" /> and they could focus their eyes independently.<ref name="G:TTOR-Y" /> A wide maw full of row upon row of yellowed,<ref name="SSC" /> needle-sharp [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]] constituted the species' only other major facial feature. The lower jaw jutted out<ref name="BTM" /> so as to allow these teeth to protrude even when the mouth was shut.<ref name="SWC 228">''[[Star Wars Chronicles]]''</ref>

The teeth betrayed the frog-dogs' [[Diet/Legends|carnivorous]] diet. Members of the species ate animals of many kinds, although [[Insect/Legends|insects]] formed the main part of their nutrition.<ref name="BTM" /> A frog-dog fed him- or herself by flicking out the long, prehensile tongue at a target. A sticky fluid allowed the tongue's bulbous tip to adhere to what it touched, so with a quick retraction, a frog-dog's surprised prey could find itself snapped up and in the frog-dog's mouth instantaneously.<ref name="TT:BT" /> Frog-dogs in captivity ate nearly anything, including moldy [[Bantha/Legends|bantha]] fat, [[gelatinous chuff]], and pieces of [[Viridian termite]] jaws.<ref name="G:TTOR-Y" />

Overall, the frog-dogs' appearance made members of other sentient species regard them as simple-minded beasts at best,<ref name="SSC" /> horrifying monsters at worst.<ref name="BTM" /><ref name="EGC 132" /> Frog-dogs had two [[Gender/Legends|sexes]], male and female.<ref name="TT:BT" /> At least one member of the species carried smaller frog-dogs in the mouth, belching them out when threatened.<ref name="SNES" /> Frog-dogs were susceptible to [[Cyborrean rabies]], a [[Disease/Legends|disease]] which manifested itself in a pink-colored frothing at the mouth.<ref name="Wolf" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|We live within a den of thieves, little one&hellip; Why do you want this?''"<br />"''For the money, of course.|B'omarr monk Evilo Nailati and Buboicullaar, on the frog-dog's decision to kill Jabba|<ref name="TT:BT" />}}
[[File:DurosFrogDogAndAurra-SWR08.jpg|thumb|right|275px|Frog-dogs blended into galactic society by playing the role of simple animals.]]
In the view of most other sentient species in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], frog-dogs seemed like non-sentient animals.<ref name="CSWE I 96" /> The squat creatures had no native technology or language,<ref name="BTM" /> and they seemed content to devote most of their time to eating and slobbering on themselves.<ref name="TT:BT" /> Some sentient beings even took frog-dogs as pets,<ref name="SWC 228" /> feeding them scraps when they begged with plaintive croaking, and keeping them harnessed and leashed with devices that fit around the frog-dog's head and forelimbs.<ref name="SSC" /><ref name="SD:TFDT">{{StoryCite|story=Skin Deep: The Fat Dancer's Tale|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}}</ref>

In reality, this was just a front. Frog-dogs were highly intelligent beings.<ref name="intelligence">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]'', the ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', and ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' all suggest that frog-dogs are highly intelligent, but the ''[[Sideshow Collectibles]]'' "Buboicullaar Creature Pack" calls them only barely intelligent. This article follows the majority of sources.</ref> Frog-dogs found it in their best interest to hide their intelligence from others.<ref name="CSWE I 296" /> This afforded them regular access to food&mdash;they could eat scraps and crumbs or even something more appealing, like a [[Jawa/Legends|Jawa]]<ref name="TT:BT" />&mdash;and it enhanced their usefulness as [[Spy/Legends|spies]] and [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]], thus providing them with employment.<ref name="CSWE I 296" /> Frog-dogs understood the value of [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] and honored contracts such as [[Bounty/Legends|bounties]] to which they had agreed.<ref name="TT:BT" />

Despite their lack of language, frog-dogs communicated their emotions via hisses, whines,<ref name="G:TTOR-Y" /> croaks of laughter,<ref name="TT:BT" /> and a {{Audio|Frog-dogCall.flac|distinctive cry}} that sounded like a cross between a bark and a croak.<ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> Their vocalizations could be both loud<ref name="Bubo CCG">{{CCG|set=Jabba's Palace Limited|cardname=Bubo}}</ref> and throaty.<ref name="RY DB">{{DB|character|reeyees|Ree-Yees}}</ref> Some members of the species had both a common name, known to outsiders, and a formal name, revealed only to close confidants. Frog-dogs relied heavily on their tongues to interact with the world around them; they tasted people to get a feel for them, as they could tell a great deal about a person by their flavor. The tongue also expressed emotion: curling in disgust, or tickling the roof of the mouth with joy.<ref name="TT:BT" />

Frog-dogs at rest often lay with the belly on the ground and the legs splayed,<ref name="ROTJ" /> but some also stood upright with the tail held outstretched.<ref name="SWR:O" /> They moved by shuffling on their two legs<ref name="TT:BT" /> or by hopping.<ref name="SNES" /> Despite this form of locomotion, frog-dogs could move with great stealth.<ref name="BTM" /> If threatened, frog-dogs could fight by biting with their sharp teeth and shaking its opponent back and forth.<ref name="HTHTT 36" />

==History==
{{Quote|What's so funny, little one?''"<br />"''I ate the detonation link, my teacher. The crucial part in Ree-Yees's plan.|B'omarr monk Evilo Nailati and Buboicullaar|<ref name="TT:BT" />}}
[[File:BoboOnLeash-RotJAVA.png|thumb|left|250px|The frog-dog Buboicullaar lived as "Bubo," a pet to a tribe of Jawas, even allowing them to keep him on a leash. In reality, Buboicullaar was secretly plotting to kill Jabba the Hutt.]]
As early as the period after the signing of the [[Treaty of Coruscant]], frog-dogs were known in the galaxy. At the [[Time/Legends|time]], a [[Huttball/Legends|Huttball]] sports team took its name from the two-legged species. The [[Frog-dogs]] played a game against a rival team, the [[Rotworms]], on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler's]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]].<ref name="HB">{{TORweb|url=info/media/trailers/huttball|text=Trailer - Huttball}}</ref>

Frog-dogs at large in the galaxy often found employ as assassins and spies,<ref name="CSWE I 296" /> occupations in which they took advantage of the fact that other sentients often took them for non-sentient beasts.<ref name="TT:BT" /> Other members of the species worked as watchbeasts, keeping guard for intruders on their employers' property.<ref name="Bubo CCG" />

Frog-dogs were present in the [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] Tatooine by [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].<ref name="SWR:O" /> In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="Date">The events of "[[Lone Wolf: A Tale of Obi-Wan and Luke]]" occur during those of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], which ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates to [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].</ref> frog-dogs were among the species present on Nar Shaddaa. Three rabid members of the species were kept leashed by ''[[go-zeki]]'', [[Gangster/Legends|gangsters]] of the [[Kyuzo/Legends|Kyuzo]] species, and pitted against the fugitive [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], who [[Death/Legends|killed]] all three with his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]].<ref name="Wolf" /> Years later, a frog-dog had joined the court of [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]] in his [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|palace]] on the desert world.<ref name="Jabba the Hutt: Betrayal">This frog-dog is visible in ''[[Jabba the Hutt: Betrayal]]''. It is unclear whether this individual is supposed to be Buboicullaar or another member of the species.</ref>

[[Buboicullaar/Legends|Buboicullaar]], known to the members of Jabba's court as Bubo, lived in the Hutt's palace in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]. He was considered the pet of a tribe of Jawas and given the official role of Jabba's personal watchbeast,<ref name="WWIJP 86" /> tasked with alerting the court to anyone entering the throne room.<ref name="RY DB" /> When the [[Droid/Legends|droids]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] arrived in the palace in 4 ABY&mdash;and the [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] kicked him&mdash;Bubo announced their presence by giving a throaty croak.<ref name="ROTJ" /> The [[Gran/Legends|Gran]] [[Ree-Yees/Legends|Ree-Yees]] was placed in charge of the frog-dog's feeding and care,<ref name="EGC 132" /><ref name="RY TCG">{{SWGTCG|set=Galactic Hunters|cardname=Ree-Yees}}</ref> which prompted him to use Bubo in an attempt to kill Jabba. The Gran hid a demolitions transmitter among Bubo's flaps of skin.<ref name="CSWE III 89">{{CSWECite|III|89|Ree-Yees}}</ref> Nevertheless, Bubo hated his keeper,<ref name="TT:BT" /> and he ate the device, foiling Ree-Yees's plan.<ref name="Bubo CCG" />

Bubo played up the misconception that he was non-sentient<ref name="CSWE I 96" /> because, in reality, he was a spy and assassin who had been contracted to kill the Hutt;<ref name="TT:BT" /> playing dumb allowed him unfettered access to the palace and proximity to his target. During his stay, Bubo befriended the [[B'omarr Order/Legends|B'omarr monks]] who roamed the palace halls in [[B'omarr brain walker|brain walkers]].<ref name="BTM" /> The frog-dog studied under the guidance of the monk [[Evilo Nailati]],<ref name="TT:BT" /> and the monks were the only inhabitants of the palace to whom Bubo revealed his sentience. After Jabba was killed by the [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] during the [[Battle of the Great Pit of Carkoon]], Bubo gave up his life as an assassin and voluntarily allowed the B'omarr monks to remove his [[Brain/Legends|brain]] from his cranium and place it in a brain walker. In this form, he spent his time pondering philosophy and the universe.<ref name="WWIJP 86" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Bubo_behind_the_scenes.jpg|thumb|right|The frog-dog costume used for ''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'' fit over its performer's torso and head; the puppeteer's legs were hidden under a false floor.]]
[[Industrial Light & Magic]] created the frog-dog Bubo as one of the background [[Alien/Legends|aliens]] for Jabba's Palace in the film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], which was first released in [[1983]]. The prototype maquette for the creature had a more upright stance than the final creation, standing on his two legs and not dragging the ground. The final character was a suit worn on the upper half of an actor's body while the performer's legs were hidden in a false floor. In the decades since the film's release, Bubo has often been confused with another creature seen in the film, the [[Worrt/Legends|worrt]]. The two are members of different species.<ref name="BTM" />

Frog-dogs appear in the [[1994]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Super Star Wars: Return of the Jedi]]'' as enemy characters in levels representing Jabba the Hutt's dance hall and his palace. The game allows the player to take on the role of [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], Leia Organa, or [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] for these stages. The boss enemy of the Jabba's Palace level is a giant frog-dog who spits smaller frog-dogs from its mouth. Because these events conflict with those of the ''Return of the Jedi'' film, this article treats them as non-canonical.<ref name="Chee">This is in keeping with Leland Chee's explanation of canon levels: {{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=488#13131496|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2005-10-25|time=9:28 AM}}</ref>

[[File:SROTJ_giant_frog-dog.png|thumb|left|thumb|250px|The video game ''Super Star Wars: Return of the Jedi'' features a giant frog-dog as the boss enemy for the Jabba's Palace level.]]
Author [[Daryl F. Mallett]] expanded on Bubo's backstory in his [[1996]] short story ''[[Tongue-tied: Bubo's Tale]]'', providing his full name&mdash;Buboicullaar&mdash;and revealing him to be a frog-dog. Mallett was also the first author to establish the species' sentience. Nevertheless, the ''[[Jabba's Palace Limited]]'' expansion of the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]] treats Bubo as a non-sentient creature rather than an intelligent character. Other sources have followed Mallett's designation. In the story ''[[Goatgrass: The Tale of Ree-Yees]]'', author [[Deborah J. Ross|Deborah Wheeler]] calls the character "a bubo" at one point, although it is unknown if this is a mistake or if "bubo" is a general term for all frog-dogs.

Bubo has since appeared in various adaptations of ''Return of the Jedi'', including the [[Return of the Jedi 1|''Marvel'' comics version]] and the [[Star Wars Manga: Return of the Jedi 1|manga adaptation]]. Similarly, frog-dogs have become fixtures of Jabba's court in stories such as ''[[Jabba the Hutt: Betrayal]]'' and ''[[Star Wars Infinities: The Empire Strikes Back]]'', wherein they appear but play no major role.
